issues.legal_issue: Expenditure incurred to complete development work under liabilities assumed with a purchased business is deductible as business expenditure when it facilitates the business and is not shown to form part of the purchase consideration.
material_facts: A company purchased an entire running land-development business, including its assets and liabilities.
Before the purchase, the firm had sold plots but had not completed promised development work; the company assumed the obligation to complete it.
The company incurred expenditure on development work for those plots as part of an integrated scheme that also covered land it sold itself.
There was nothing to show that the assumed development obligation was quantified or included in the consideration for the business transfer.
issues.conclusion: The expenditure incurred in discharging the assumed development obligations was allowable as a deduction in computing the company's business profits.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(2)(xv) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, expenditure may be deductible where it is laid out wholly and exclusively for business purposes. Revenue expenditure is not confined to expenditure on stock-in-trade: expenditure voluntarily incurred on grounds of commercial expediency to facilitate the carrying on of a business may qualify. The Court applied Eastern Investments Ltd. v. CIT, 20 I.T.R. 1, and Cooke (H.M. Inspector of Taxes) v. Quick Shoe Repair Service, 30 T.C. 460. It distinguished Royal Insurance Company v. Watson, 3 T.C. 500, because the assumed obligation was not shown to have been quantified as part of the purchase price, and referred to CIT (Central), Calcutta v. Mugneeram Bangur & Co. (Land Department), 57 I.T.R. 299.

rule.if: income_tax_business_expense_claim and purchased_running_business_with_liabilities and assumed_preexisting_business_obligation and obligation_facilitates_business and integrated_development_scheme and not obligation_quantified_as_purchase_consideration

predicates.income_tax_business_expense_claim: The matter is an income-tax assessment in which a taxpayer seeks to deduct expenditure incurred in carrying on a business.
predicates.purchased_running_business_with_liabilit: The taxpayer acquired a running business together with its liabilities.
predicates.assumed_preexisting_business_obligation: The taxpayer assumed an outstanding obligation arising from the business before its acquisition.
predicates.obligation_facilitates_business: Discharging the obligation facilitates the taxpayer's conduct of the business.
predicates.integrated_development_scheme: The work required to discharge the obligation forms part of a unified development scheme that cannot practicably be divided among individual properties.
predicates.obligation_quantified_as_purchase_consid: The assumed obligation was quantified and included as part of the consideration paid to acquire the business.

issues.definition: When an income-tax business-expense claim concerns an assumed pre-existing business obligation that facilitates an integrated business scheme, and that obligation was not quantified as purchase consideration, the expense is deductible as business expenditure.

issues.legal_issue: Consideration that a purchaser has not paid and has merely secured by a mortgage is not treated as income received by the seller.
material_facts: The company sold plots for a price payable partly in cash and partly in future instalments.
The purchasers secured the unpaid balances by mortgages over the plots sold.
The purchasers had not paid those balances during the assessment periods in question.
issues.conclusion: The unpaid balances secured by mortgages were not taxable as income received during the assessment periods.
issues.legal_principle: A security for a debt is not equivalent to payment or receipt of the debt. The Court relied on Commissioner of Income-tax, Bihar & Orissa v. Maharajadhiraja of Darbhanga, 60 I.A. 146, which held that a debtor's promissory note for an amount owed was not the equivalent of cash payment or receipt. Applying that principle, the mere execution of mortgage deeds securing deferred sale consideration did not amount to constructive receipt of income.

rule.if: income_tax_receipt_assessment and sale_consideration_part_deferred and purchaser_not_paid_deferred_balance and deferred_balance_secured_by_mortgage and mortgage_is_only_security_for_debt

predicates.income_tax_receipt_assessment: The matter is an income-tax assessment in which the timing or receipt of income is disputed.
predicates.sale_consideration_part_deferred: A seller transferred property for consideration payable partly at once and partly in the future.
predicates.purchaser_not_paid_deferred_balance: The purchaser had not paid the deferred balance during the relevant assessment period.
predicates.deferred_balance_secured_by_mortgage: The purchaser secured the unpaid balance by a mortgage over the transferred property.
predicates.mortgage_is_only_security_for_debt: The mortgage served only as security for the debt and did not itself satisfy or discharge that debt.

issues.definition: In an income-tax receipt assessment, an unpaid deferred sale balance that is secured only by a mortgage is not taxable as income received.
